meaning: One recorded attempt at the task; on disk, rows in a shared Parquet file plus frames in shared MP4 files.
Putting the scene back (the block and the cup) between two recorded episodes.
A gripper with a camera on it that a person holds to do the task without a robot; software reconstructs the gripper's path afterwards.
The 2024 project that introduced the hand-held gripper with a camera as a way to record demonstrations without a robot.
The on-disk layout LeRobot v0.7.0 writes: Parquet files of rows, MP4 files of camera frames, and metadata, with many episodes per file.
A compressed, column-by-column table file format; LeRobot stores the per-tick rows in it.
The files that describe a dataset's schema and say where each episode sits inside the shared data and video files.
The five columns the recorder fills in on every row: timestamp, frame_index, episode_index, index and task_index.
A numbered folder (chunk-000) that holds up to 1,000 data or video files by default.
The site where LeRobot datasets and models are published.
A method for compressing video into a file (the encoder half) and turning it back into frames (the decoder half).
The program or circuit that compresses video at recording time; a different thing from the joint-angle encoder of section 3.
The program or circuit that turns compressed video back into frames each time the data is read.
A video frame stored whole, which can be decoded on its own; other frames are stored as differences.
The spacing of keyframes in a video; a GOP of 2 means a keyframe every second frame, which makes reading a random frame cheap.
The encoder's quality dial: one number for how much detail it may discard; lower means better quality and larger files.
A video compression standard; the codec LeRobot v0.7.0 writes by default.
A software encoder for AV1 that runs on CPU cores; libsvtav1 is its name in LeRobot's settings.
Another video compression standard; the alternative LeRobot offers in software and through hardware encoders.
Another video compression standard, also called H.265, available through LeRobot's hardware encoders.
A fixed circuit in a GPU or processor that compresses video without loading the CPU cores.
A recorder option that encodes frames during capture, in place of writing PNG images and encoding after the episode.
The time at which an episode begins inside a camera's shared MP4 file; added to a row's timestamp to find its frame.
The rate the recorder was asked to run at (30 fps by default); timestamps are computed from it, whatever rate the loop achieved.
Recording in which a trained policy drives the arm and a person takes over before a failure, so the recovery becomes training data.
An action that gives the pose of the gripper, which must be converted into joint angles before an arm can follow it (built in section 3).
A LeRobot encoder setting that picks the first hardware encoder the host offers and falls back to SVT-AV1 when there is none.
The dataset call that closes the Parquet writers; without it the Parquet files are corrupt.
